label: miso 86 netrev margin
definition: KEEPER (determination NOT-YET). SINGLE delta on the 2026-07-20-miso-81-phantom-outage recipe: gas_offer_margin=true — the go-forward fuel-invariant $/MWh net-revenue gas offer form (anchor 3.0492 $/MMBtu, a measured constant), replacing the fuel-scaled heat-rate-multiplier markup. Outages stay on the CAMPD unit-level derate: the MISO-native published outage overlay was solved and scored first (2026-07-24-miso-85-dam-outage) and rejected on GRAIN — MISO publishes region × cause daily MW with no unit or fuel identity. Full span 2023–2025, per-year chained, zero fitted scalars.
market_story: The net-revenue margin is a bid-structure change, not a dispatch lever: MISO's gas fleet offers a fixed $/MWh margin over its own delivered-fuel cost rather than a fuel-scaled multiple of it, which is how a merchant CC actually bids — it needs the same $/MWh contribution to fixed cost whether gas is $2.49 or $3.82. The form is two-sided about the 3.0492 $/MMBtu anchor: in the below-anchor years (2023 gas 2.84, 2024 2.49) it FIRMS the offer up, in the above-anchor year (2025 3.82) it COMPRESSES it down, and at anchor it reduces exactly to the registered band multipliers. The visible cost is one marginal crossing: the 2023 firming sheds ~0.86 TWh of CC_REGULAR dispatch, taking C1 from −7.76 to −8.62 TWh against a ±8.0 band, and 2025's compression takes C3b monthly-NRMSE from 0.194 to 0.204 against a ≤0.20 veto. Both are recorded as MODEL MISSes, not calibrated away — the form is kept because it is the structurally faithful bid, not because it scores better (rule 1). What it does NOT touch is MISO's known frontier: the {C3a-2025, C3c} scarcity tail is an administrative ORDC/RCPF construct derived from a Monte-Carlo LOLP simulation that a deterministic perfect-foresight hourly LP does not contain (miso-82, externally validated), so it stays ledgered exactly as adjudicated on the miso-81 keeper.
